whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.intro: Here you connect your own WhatsApp. UCAP then becomes one of its linked devices, like WhatsApp Web: it reads your messages to you and sends replies after you confirmed them. This gives your helpers no access to your messages.
whatsapp.risk: Before you connect: WhatsApp does not allow other programs. UCAP connects anyway, the way WhatsApp Web does. Meta may block your number for it, even if you write little. Then you can no longer use WhatsApp with this number, not even on your phone. If you do not want that, do not connect WhatsApp.
whatsapp.agree: I understand the risk: connect WhatsApp
whatsapp.notAllowed: WhatsApp is not allowed on this server. The administration can allow it.
whatsapp.notRunning: The server's WhatsApp service is not running right now. Try again later.
whatsapp.state.wait_phone: Enter your WhatsApp's number with its country code, for example +49 170 1234567.
whatsapp.state.wait_pairing: Open WhatsApp on your phone: Settings, Linked devices, Link a device. Choose "Link with phone number instead" there and type the code. WhatsApp may also show you a notification for it.
whatsapp.code.label: Code for WhatsApp: {chars}
whatsapp.code.where: In WhatsApp, UCAP is then called "Chrome (Mac OS)" in the list of linked devices.

whatsapp.state.closed: The connection has ended. "Reconnect" starts it again.
whatsapp.state.logged_out: UCAP was removed from your linked devices. "Reconnect" links it again.
whatsapp.error.phone_number_invalid: That is no number with a country code. For example: +49 170 1234567.
whatsapp.error.pairing_expired: The code has expired: WhatsApp waits only about three minutes for it. Get a new one.
whatsapp.error.pairing_failed: WhatsApp gave no code. Get a new one.
whatsapp.error.login_timeout: Connecting took too long and was stopped.
whatsapp.error.forbidden: WhatsApp refused the connection. The number may be blocked.
whatsapp.disconnect.confirm: Disconnect WhatsApp? UCAP is removed from your linked devices, and the copies of your messages on this server are deleted. WhatsApp keeps its own.
whatsapp.disconnected.manual: WhatsApp is disconnected on this server. Remove UCAP on your phone as well: WhatsApp, Linked devices, "Chrome (Mac OS)", Log out.
email.title: Email
email.intro: Here you connect an email account. UCAP reads your emails to you and sends replies after you confirm them. Your helpers get no access to your emails through this.

email.hint.appPassword.gmail: Gmail needs an app password, not your Google password. It only exists with 2-Step Verification: you create it in your Google Account, under Security, App passwords.
email.hint.appPassword.icloud: iCloud needs an app-specific password, not your Apple password. You create it in your Apple Account, under Sign-In and Security.
email.hint.appPassword.tonline: Telekom needs a separate email password for other programs, not the password of your Telekom login. You create it in Telekom's email centre, in the settings under passwords.
email.hint.enableImap: {name} needs access for other programs switched on first: in the mailbox under Settings, POP3 and IMAP.

sms.title: Text messages
sms.intro: Here UCAP becomes this phone's SMS app. Then UCAP receives and sends your text messages itself, and Android keeps them as before: Google Messages finds them again if you switch back to it later. Your helpers get no access to your text messages through this.
sms.unavailable: Text messages are only available in the UCAP app on a phone with a SIM card.
sms.state.other: Your SMS app is {app} right now.
sms.state.none: This phone has no SMS app right now.
sms.state.held: UCAP is this phone's SMS app, but not yet connected to your account.
sms.state.ready: UCAP is this phone's SMS app. UCAP has your text messages of the last 30 days and all new ones.
sms.rcs: Before UCAP becomes your SMS app: switch off Google Messages' chat features (Google Messages, Settings, Chat features). Otherwise chats people send you there may stop arriving.
sms.dialog: Android then asks you itself: choose UCAP in the list, then “Set as default”.
sms.take: Use UCAP as the SMS app
sms.restricted: If Android does not offer this and UCAP was installed from a file: open UCAP's app info, tap the menu at the top right and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then try again.
sms.refused: UCAP did not become the SMS app. If Android did not ask: what helps then is below.
sms.connected: UCAP is now your SMS app. Your text messages of the last 30 days are being transferred, and all new ones will follow.
sms.giveBack.what: You can switch back to another SMS app at any time, such as Google Messages. Your text messages stay on the phone.
sms.giveBack: Switch back to another SMS app
sms.giveBack.how: Android opens the default apps. Tap “SMS app” and choose Google Messages.
